info.title: kono-router
info.description: OpenAI-compatible free-inference router. Chat and image routes never fail: after an exhaustive endpoint sweep they return 200 with `kono.degraded=true` (buffered responses also set `X-Kono-Degraded: 1`; streams send headers before routing settles, so they signal it in-band). Every request is traced: `traceparent` is honoured inbound and returned outbound, spans are exported via OpenTelemetry and kept in a per-isolate ring under `/v1/traces`. The ASCK-T tool plane adds first-class tool support: `GET /v1/tools` lists executable built-ins (calculation, data/JSON, text, time, crypto, durable files, clipboard, tasks, memory, RAG, embeddings, web search/fetch, HTTP and mesh introspection) with their learned reliability, `POST /v1/tools/execute` runs them directly, and a chat request can attach them with `"tools": "auto"` so the router executes the calls itself and loops until the model answers.

get.description: Every tool the plane can execute on a model's behalf, with its JSON Schema, aliases and learned skill record (Beta-Bernoulli success posterior, Wilson competence floor, Kalman-filtered p50/p95/p99 latency, repair rate and top error codes). `wire.tools` is the same registry projected onto a vendor tool-call format, ready to paste into a chat request. post.summary: Execute tool calls server-side
post.description: Runs one call (`{name, arguments}`) or a batch (`{calls:[...]}`) and returns each result with the parse strategy and the repairs the argument ladder applied. Accepts OpenAI nesting (`function.name` / `function.arguments`) as well as flat `{name, arguments}`. Every execution updates the tool's skill memory, so direct calls teach the plane too. Always returns 200: a failing tool is reported per-call with `ok:false` and a machine-readable `code`, which is what a model needs in order to retry.

200.description: Per-call results; the request itself never fails

post.summary: Chat completion (JSON or SSE)

200.description: Completion. With stream=true, headers and a `: trace <id>` comment are sent immediately, `: routing` heartbeats follow every 5 s until an upstream commits, then chunks stream in real time: `delta.reasoning_content` (including leading inline <think> blocks), `delta.content`, `delta.tool_calls` (stable index; id and type on each call's first chunk). The final chunk carries `kono`. No response stays silent longer than KONO_IDLE_MS (default 15 s): streams send `: keepalive` comments whenever nothing else has been sent (a quiet upstream, a server-side tool round); buffered responses still unfinished at that point commit the 200 and send whitespace (valid before JSON) until the body is ready, so their timing headers move into `kono`/`telemetry`.

Plan, execute and answer with a compiled tool DAG
post.description: LLMCompiler-style agent over the tool plane. BM25 retrieves the relevant tools; `samples` plans are drawn in parallel at spread temperatures and the minimum-Bayes-risk plan (expected Jaccard utility over id-free call signatures, down-weighted by literal schema failures) is executed as a DAG: list scheduling by upward rank over learned tool latencies, bounded concurrency, `$n1.path` / `${n1.path}` result references, stateful tools chained in order, dependents of a failed node skipped. A joiner answers or requests a replan (up to `rounds`). Sub-calls run in-process through this router as the caller (same key, session and quota) and nest in one trace.

post.summary: MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint (JSON-RPC)
post.description: Model Context Protocol Streamable HTTP transport, protocolVersion 2025-03-26. Methods: initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call. Batch requests are rejected with JSON-RPC error -32600. Tool failures are returned as isError content in the result, never as transport errors. Public envelope: no bearer auth on the endpoint itself; internal work is metered.

post.summary: A2A agent JSON-RPC endpoint
post.description: Agent2Agent (A2A) JSON-RPC endpoint. Methods: message/send, message/stream (SSE), tasks/get, tasks/cancel, tasks/resubscribe. Tasks are persisted in KV for 24h and are owner-scoped: unknown or foreign task ids return TaskNotFound (-32001). Push notifications are not supported. Public envelope: no bearer auth on the endpoint itself; internal work is metered.

200.description: JSON-RPC result: a Task or Message. With message/stream, an SSE stream of task/status/artifact events.

schema.description: `data: <JSON-RPC response>` frames carrying Task, status-update and artifact-update events

400.description: Invalid JSON-RPC request, or TaskNotFound (-32001) for unknown or foreign task ids

get.description: Public A2A agent card for this router: name, skills, capabilities (streaming; push notifications not supported) and the /a2a JSON-RPC endpoint URL.

post.summary: OpenAI Responses API adapter over chat completions
post.description: OpenAI Responses API surface backed by the chat-completions router. `input` is a string or an array of items; `instructions` sets the system prompt. `previous_response_id` continues a chain whose state is stored for 24h in KV. Streaming emits response.created, response.output_text.delta and response.completed events. Degraded upstreams produce a response with status failed and error code upstream_degraded instead of a fabricated answer.

input.description: Input text, or an array of input items.

previous_response_id.description: Id of a previous response (stored 24h in KV) to continue from.

200.description: Response object. With stream=true, SSE events: response.created, response.output_text.delta, response.completed; a degraded upstream completes with status failed and error code upstream_degraded.

get.summary: Read the caller's live conversation
get.description: Returns the stored live conversation for the session identified by the `x-kono-session` header (fallback `x-session-id`): `{saved, messages}`. Conversations are scoped to the sha256 of the session id. 404 when nothing is stored; 400 when the session header is missing.

404.description: No conversation stored for this session.

put.description: Overwrites the live conversation for the session identified by the `x-kono-session` header (fallback `x-session-id`). Body: `{saved, messages}` with at most 2000 messages, each an object with a string `role`; bodies over ~5 MB are rejected with 413.

400.description: Missing session header or invalid messages.

get.summary: List the caller's saved conversation snapshots
get.description: Returns `{items: [{id, title, saved, count}]}` for the session identified by the `x-kono-session` header (fallback `x-session-id`); empty when the library is empty.

post.summary: Save a conversation snapshot to the library
post.description: Stores a snapshot `{id?, title, saved, messages}` (same validation as the live conversation) for the session identified by the `x-kono-session` header (fallback `x-session-id`). The id is generated when omitted. The library holds at most 30 snapshots; the oldest by `saved` are evicted.

400.description: Missing session header or invalid messages.

get.summary: Read one saved conversation snapshot
get.description: Returns the full snapshot `{id, title, saved, session?, messages}` for the session identified by the `x-kono-session` header (fallback `x-session-id`); 404 when the id is unknown to this session.

delete.description: Removes the snapshot and its library index entry for the session identified by the `x-kono-session` header (fallback `x-session-id`). Idempotent: deleting an unknown id still returns {ok: true}.

post.summary: Multi-agent run: plan, parallel workers, verify, synthesize
post.description: One multi-agent run over this router: a planner decomposes the task, workers execute the steps in parallel, a verifier checks the results and a synthesizer writes the final answer. Bounded at 11 internal chat calls per run. With stream=true the run returns AG-UI events: RUN_STARTED, STEP_STARTED, TOOL_CALL_START, TOOL_CALL_RESULT, TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT, RUN_FINISHED, RUN_ERROR.

messages.description: Alternative to input: the last user message is the task.

stream.description: Stream AG-UI events instead of a buffered result.

example.input: Research the options and draft a recommendation.

200.description: Run result. With stream=true, an SSE stream of AG-UI events (RUN_STARTED, STEP_STARTED, TOOL_CALL_START, TOOL_CALL_RESULT, TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT, RUN_FINISHED, RUN_ERROR).

reliabilityDraw.description: Thompson sample from discounted Beta posterior

toolCompetence.description: Wilson floor on this tuple's learned ability to emit valid tool calls; 0 while unproven

current_best_tools.description: Smart lane ranked by learned tool-call competence

ChatRequest.description: Malformed bodies are normalised, never rejected. Any model id is accepted: free:* aliases select a mode, unknown ids route by trigram/Jaccard similarity.

tools.description: OpenAI tool declarations, or the string "auto" to attach the router's built-in tools and let it execute the calls itself.

kono_tools.description: Attach built-in tools alongside any client tools: true/"auto" for the default set, "all" for every non-admin tool, or a comma/space separated list of names. Equivalent to the x-kono-tools request header.

kono_preamble.description: Prepend a one-line system message describing the attached tools. Set false to leave the message list untouched.

kono_rounds.description: Server-side agent rounds for tools:"auto" (default KONO_TOOL_ROUNDS, 8). The build gate extends it while it sends the agent back to work.

kono_gate.description: Build gate. When an agent turn changed the session workspace, the final answer is checked: static diagnostics, runtime errors of the current files and app_test results (and, with a test runner, that a test run passed against the current files). While anything is unmet the findings go back to the agent as a user turn and the loop continues (status frame `kono.type = build_gate` on streams). false disables it; "always" checks even when nothing changed.

kono_gate_rounds.description: Most times the build gate may send the agent back in one request.

kono_runner.description: The client runs app_test jobs in a browser (the dashboard's hidden preview, via the admin app_runner tool) for the duration of this request. Lets app_test wait for results and makes the gate require a passing test run.

arguments.description: JSON text; object arguments from upstreams are serialised

tool_rounds.description: Server-side tool rounds executed before this answer (absent when 0)

tools_executed.description: One entry per executed call: round, tool name, ok and ms

repaired.description: True when the arguments had to be repaired (declared defaults do not count)

items.description: One entry per executed call: round, tool name, ok, ms, repaired and any failure code/text

ToolSpec.description: One executable tool plus everything learned about it.

aliases.description: Accepted alternative spellings (dotted, kebab, camelCase, synonyms)

admin.description: Requires x-admin-secret; never advertised to models

parameters.description: JSON Schema (2020-12 subset) for the arguments object

skill.description: null until the tool has been executed at least once

ToolSkill.description: Compounding skill memory for one tool: a discounted Beta-Bernoulli success posterior and a Kalman filter over ln(latency).

competence.description: Wilson lower bound - the honest, evidence-weighted reliability floor

competence_draw.description: Thompson sample the router ranks on

repair_rate.description: Share of calls whose arguments needed the repair ladder

session.description: Namespace used for every stateful tool (fs_*, memory_*, rag_*, clipboard, task)

max_rounds.description: KONO_TOOL_ROUNDS; 0 disables the server-side agent loop

ToolExecuteRequest.description: Either a single call or a batch. Both OpenAI nesting and flat keys are accepted.

arguments.description: Object, or a JSON string as emitted by a model (the repair ladder parses it)

id.description: Echoed back so a batch can be correlated

strategy.description: Which rung of the argument ladder produced the call

ok.description: true only when every call succeeded

error.description: Only when the request body itself was unusable
